plan.contextChunk: This figure is an isometric schematic of a deep network drawn as a tall rectangular box standing on end between two labeled faces. The word Data sits below the bottom face and the word Embedding sits above the top face. Inside, three light gray parallelogram planes are stacked at even heights to stand for intermediate layers, with the box's outer edges in solid black and the interior planes outlined in a lighter gray. Five dotted curves thread up through the stack, each starting at a filled round dot on or near the lower planes and ending in an arrowhead just short of the top face, so a single datapoint can be traced through every layer. A long vertical arrow at the far left points upward beside the rotated text Representation learning, and a matching arrow at the far right points downward beside Generative modeling. The two opposed arrows carry the encoding: the same stack of layers is read bottom-up in one case and top-down in the other. The picture sets up the claim that representation learning and generative modeling are two readings of one architecture, and invites the question of what actually separates data from an embedding.

elements: outer rectangular box (12 solid black edges) standing tall on end
bottom face of the box (the 'Data' plane)
top face of the box (the 'Embedding' plane)
three light-gray semi-transparent parallelogram planes stacked at even heights inside the box (intermediate layers), outlined in lighter gray
five dotted curves threading vertically through the stack, each beginning at a filled round dot near the bottom and ending in an arrowhead just below the top face
five filled round dots at the lower ends of the dotted curves, scattered in (x,z) on/near the lowest plane
five arrowheads at the upper ends of the dotted curves near the top face
long vertical arrow at far left pointing UP beside rotated text 'Representation learning'
long vertical arrow at far right pointing DOWN beside rotated text 'Generative modeling'
label 'Data' centered below the bottom face
label 'Embedding' centered above the top face

interactions.label: Reading direction
interactions.teaches: The identical stack of layers is read bottom-up (data -> embedding) for representation learning and top-down (embedding -> data) for generative modeling; reversing the toggle flips every dotted path's arrowhead and animation direction, making the two views opposite readings of one architecture

interactions.label: Layer traversal
interactions.teaches: Stepping one plane at a time highlights the current layer and the locations of the five points on it, showing how each datapoint's position (its representation) changes as it passes through successive layers
Rotating the box confirms the planes are genuinely stacked in 3D and that the dotted paths pierce every layer, not merely drawn on a flat diagram

demo_steps.title: Representation learning, at Data
demo_steps.narration: Direction = Representation learning, traversal at the Data plane. The bottom plane and the five source dots are highlighted; dotted arrows point upward toward Embedding.

demo_steps.title: Climb to Layer 2
demo_steps.narration: Step the traversal to Layer 2. The middle plane lights up and the five markers slide to their Layer-2 positions, illustrating the representation changing layer by layer.

demo_steps.title: Reach the Embedding
demo_steps.narration: At the Embedding plane the markers reach their topmost, most abstract positions; the upward arrows terminate here.

demo_steps.title: Flip to Generative modeling
demo_steps.narration: Switch the reading direction. The same stack is now traversed top-down: arrowheads reverse to point downward and the animation flows from Embedding back to Data.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World box: width X ~3 units (+X screen-right), depth Z ~3 units (+Z receding diagonal), height Y ~4 units (+Y up). Bottom face at y=0, top face at y=4. Three interior gray planes at y=1, y=2, y=3 (evenly spaced), each a 3x3 parallelogram matching the box footprint, fill #cccccc at ~0.28 opacity, outline #888888. Outer box edges solid #000000 linewidth ~2. Five dotted curves: start dots at y~0.25 scattered in (x,z) within the footprint (e.g. (-1,-0.6),(0.2,-1),(1,0.4),(-0.4,0.9),(0.8,-0.3)), end arrowheads at y~3.7; curves gently bow outward then converge, drawn as dark-gray #444444 dashed lines (LineDashedMaterial dashSize~0.12 gapSize~0.1). Dots are small black spheres r~0.06; arrowheads small black cones. Left up-arrow and right down-arrow are thick black vertical lines with cone heads placed outside the box at x~-2.6 and x~+2.6 spanning the box height; rotated side labels 'Representation learning' (left) and 'Generative modeling' (right); 'Data' below bottom face, 'Embedding' above top face, all black. Palette: black #000000, plane gray #cccccc, plane edge #888888, path gray #444444.
interactionPlan.notes: Use LineDashedMaterial for the five dotted paths and call computeLineDistances(). Animate direction by either reversing a moving marker sphere along each path or scrolling dashOffset; on toggle flip arrowhead cone orientation (pointing +Y for Representation learning, -Y for Generative modeling). For layerStep, lerp the five marker spheres to the per-layer (x,z,y) sample of each path and raise the active plane's material opacity/emissive while dimming others; enlarge/recolor the markers sitting on the active plane. Keep side arrows and text as screen-space or billboarded sprites so they stay legible. Hide the orbit-induced confusion by clamping polar angle so the box never flips upside-down.

authoredContext:
In the section, we described neural nets as being a
sequence of mappings from raw data to ever more abstracted
representations, layer by layer. This perspective puts representation
learning in the spotlight: deep learning is just representation
learning! Let us now point out an alternative perspective: in backward
order, deep nets are mappings from abstracted representations to ever
more concrete representations of the data, layer by layer. This backward
ordering is the direction in which deep generative networks work. This
perspective puts the spotlight on generative modeling: deep learning is
just generative modeling! Indeed both modeling directions are valid, and
the full picture looks like this
(the figure):

The relationship between representation learning and generative modeling. Here we label one side as "Data" and the other as "Embedding"; but what's the precise difference between these two things? Why is an RGB image data while a 100-dimensional vector of neural activations is an embedding? This is a question for you to think about; there is no correct answer.

evaluation.notes: Strong semantic match: correct axonometric box, three interior layers, five dotted data-to-embedding trajectories with arrowheads, and correct up/down side arrows with rotated labels; meaningful layer-traversal and direction-toggle interactions reinforce the representation-learning vs generative-modeling concept, with only minor label-placement and marker-color fidelity issues.
